en: Points of Controversy The Great Pentad The Fifteenth Chapter
The Discourse on the Instant, the Moment, and the Muhūrta:
Is the instant (khaṇa) fully established? Is the moment (laya) fully established? Is the muhūrta fully established?
Yes, it is.
“Is it form?
One should not say so … pe … “Is it feeling? … [and so on].
Perception … volitional formations … consciousness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “it is produced for a moment”?
“Yes, [it is so].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, there are these three bases for discourse’?”
Which three?
Monks, one might speak concerning the past time, saying:
"Thus it was in the past."
Or, monks, one might speak concerning the future time, saying:
"Thus will it be in the future";
or, monks, one might speak concerning the present time, saying: [thus it is now].
‘It is thus now in the present.
These, monks, are the three bases for discourse.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes, [it is].
“In that case, it must be produced momentarily.
The Discussion of Moments, Seconds, and Muhūrtas is finished.
